text.p: Turkish troops entered northern Iraq early on Wednesday to help Iraqi Kurds fight Turkish separatist Kurds, foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told reporters.

"Some of our troops entered the region...in the direction of Zakho," Atacanli said. "(Iraqi Kurdish leader Massoud) Barzani began an operation against the PKK this morning, our troops have been going into northern Iraq to support this operation."
Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), which controls the northwestern section of Kurdish-run northern Iraq, has asked Turkey for help, Atacanli said.
He said the Turkish participation in the operation against the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) was "limited", but troops might take part in clashes as necessary, he said.

Witnesses said around 3,000 troops, with tanks and artillery, pushed across the border early on Wednesday. The assault, which began at 2300 GMT, followed a security sweep by local KDP authorities, who ordered all journalists to leave the border region and confiscated mobile telephones capable of reaching Turkey.
